flags.text: An AI literature-search tool read abstracts (about 20 in a smaller run and about 100 in a larger run), not full texts; evidence labels were assigned from abstracts.
flags.implication_for_page: Show a methods note near any evidence label.

flags.text: Smaller and larger runs with the same prompt cite largely different papers (198 distinct papers across the three larger runs; only 9, 9 and 14 overlap with the smaller runs). Smaller-run results sample a different slice of the literature.
flags.implication_for_page: Prefer larger-run content; label smaller-run-only content as scoping.

flags.text: Evidence-strength scores in claims are an AI literature-search tool's own judgments, not validated measures.
The "retrieved" counts differ by a factor of about 35 between similar runs and are not a coverage measure.
Research-gap matrices came out with empty cells in the saved documents.
flags.implication_for_page: Use the gaps in gaps.json instead.

flags.text: Timeline figures in several outputs plot publication dates and counts of the supporting papers, not historical milestones.
Evidence is concentrated in the Global North, in English, and in Europe and North America; Britain dominates historical archives. Several outputs say so explicitly.
flags.implication_for_page: Show a geographic coverage caveat on regional views.

flags.text: Cited sources include preprints, book reviews, editorials, conference proceedings, working papers and low-visibility venues. an AI literature-search tool flags some of them.
flags.implication_for_page: Use papers.json venue_flag; avoid load-bearing claims on flagged items.

flags.text: A few papers carry much of the weight (one workshop study cited 23 times in run-4c; Bayne and Ross 26 times and Komljenovic et al. 25 times in run-3d). The scenario map rests on few studies.
flags.implication_for_page: Show source counts next to scenarios.

flags.text: Quadrant placement and winners and losers are interpretive mappings by an AI literature-search tool, not classifications used by the original authors; several typologies could not be placed.

Horizon tables classify by the interval a study or scenario covers, not by distance from today; publication year is not a target date; some scenario sets are undated and non-predictive. The saved horizons are not a basis for 5/10/15/20-year statements.
The first prompt prioritised systematic reviews and meta-analyses, which favoured course-level interventions (digitalization IN HE).
The micro prompt named doctoral candidates and apprenticeship of junior researchers; that wording was an AI model's, so doctoral material reflects prompt design. Doctoral training is out of scope.
flags.implication_for_page: Treat doctoral material as degree-structure evidence only.

flags.text: The output contains a stray sentence unrelated to the topic (about CRISPR).
Run 7b did not capture the researcher's ecosystem; it returned innovation-ecosystem vocabulary and recent eras only. Use runs 8a-8c.
flags.implication_for_page: Do not use E01-E10 as the ecosystem story.

flags.text: an AI literature-search tool flags an SSRN preprint on Orientalism, editorials, book reviews, incompletely identified records, a Nature record dated 2019 that describes a Soviet-era relocation (chronology to verify), and a European-Iran comparison with developmental framing. Thin areas: Alexandria and Egyptian institutions, sabha and parishad, Tamil Sangam, Baghdad and Gondishapur continuity, several national academies.

Archival depth is concentrated in Britain; nineteenth-century international meetings are under-researched; African journal metadata are incomplete; platform founding dates for Latindex, SciELO, Redalyc and AJOL are not established; one Royal Society manuscript is under review.

A data-sharing meta-synthesis drew most studies from North America, with Europe a distant second; national-library origins, museum-university relationships and early data-archive founding dates are insufficiently documented.

No milestone has longitudinal outcome evidence; individual adoption and participation figures come from abstracts and need verification; most 2013-2015 empirical MOOC research came from North America and Europe.
The policy pass used web searches and summaries; primary documents were not read in full; one Council page was blocked; search result text is not archived verbatim.

Latin America, Sub-Saharan Africa and the Soviet sphere are sparse or limited to conference proceedings; one sentence on Soviet shares was cut off in the reading; the larger run re-run was not run (credits).

Milestone coding (levels, change type, continuity/disruption, valence, regions) is an AI model's inference from source text; levels are stated in the source only for Y-rows; 80 of 174 rows have an unclear continuity/disruption reading; researcher review is pending.
flags.implication_for_page: Expose coding_basis and confidence; do not present coding as findings.

flags.text: Some date spans were inferred by an AI model from named periods (for example dynasties, Hellenistic period; date_basis inferred_from_named_period) or come from general knowledge without a source (claude_general_knowledge_unsourced).
flags.implication_for_page: Render uncertain dates as ranges or hatched bars.

flags.text: Duplicate and superseded rows are kept for provenance and flagged canonical=false.
Some sources use civilisational, diffusionist or developmental-stage language. It is not adopted here; context is described, not ranked.
flags.implication_for_page: Avoid stage vocabulary in the page.

flags.text: Outputs from an AI literature-search tool carry a notice that results are for personal, non-commercial use and that redistribution requires copyright holders' consent. The restricted archive must not be published; the data/ files avoid verbatim long text, abstracts and extracted passages.
Valence is coded only where the source states winners or losers (26 rows); 148 of 174 are not coded.
flags.implication_for_page: Do not infer valence for uncoded rows.

flags.text: Doctoral training is a separate line of inquiry; doctoral material in the outputs is incidental.
flags.implication_for_page: Do not build a doctoral view.

flags.text: papers.json lists cited papers; entries from runs 1 and 2 were parsed approximately from reference lists. Being cited in a run does not mean endorsement, and no quality assessment of individual papers was made.
flags.implication_for_page: Describe the index as a bibliography of what the runs cited.

flags.text: Most evidence is cross-sectional or descriptive; the record contains no causal estimate of technology on university form.
